identification.summary: Storm-0062 is a Microsoft-tracked nation-state cluster (also tracked as DarkShadow and Oro0lxy by others). In October 2023 Microsoft said Storm-0062 had been exploiting the Atlassian Confluence Data Center and Server vulnerability CVE-2023-22515 in the wild since 14 September 2023 [S2][S3]. Press coverage of Microsoft's notice described the actor as China-linked [S3][S4]. The name 'Shadow Typhoon' could not be verified against a retrieved source and is treated as unconfirmed (see gaps).
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft-observed exploitation of CVE-2023-22515 began 2023-09-14 [S2][S3]. Earlier activity under this name is not established in the sources gathered.
identification.notes: The Oro0lxy alias is described by The Record as previously linked to a 2020 DOJ indictment involving China's Ministry of State Security [S4]; that link was not verified against the indictment text (see gaps).

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China (reported). SecurityWeek, citing its own sources, said the Storm-0062 team has been observed conducting cyberespionage for China's Ministry of State Security [S2]. Microsoft's October 2023 notice called the actor a nation-state actor but did not name China, according to SecurityWeek and The Record [S2][S4].
attribution.confidence: Moderate-to-low for the specific state agency. Microsoft's statement says nation-state [S2]; the MSS link rests on unnamed sources in press reporting [S2]. Dark Reading and Petri describe Microsoft as attributing to a Chinese APT, which is the outlets' characterization [S3][S4].
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Intelligence social-media posts on 2023-10-10 (reported by press; originals not retrieved) [S2][S3]; press reporting on the Oro0lxy alias [S4].

targeting.notes: Victims of the Storm-0062 Confluence exploitation were not named in the sources gathered. Atlassian said multiple customers reported attacks in which external attackers created unauthorized Confluence administrator accounts [S2]. The affected product was the on-premises Confluence Data Center and Server editions [S2][S5].

capabilities.summary: Zero-day exploitation of CVE-2023-22515, a CVSS 10 (per Atlassian/SecurityWeek; some outlets cite 9.8) broken-access-control flaw in Confluence Data Center and Server 8.0.0 through 8.5.1 that is reachable without authentication [S2][S5]. Microsoft said any device with network access to a vulnerable application could exploit it to create an administrator account [S3]. Exploitation as a zero-day ran about three weeks before Atlassian's 2023-10-04 disclosure [S2][S3]. Public proof-of-concept exploits appeared soon after [S3]. Microsoft published four IP addresses seen sending exploit traffic: 192.69.90[.]31, 104.128.89[.]92, 23.105.208[.]154 and 199.193.127[.]231 [S3]. Post-exploitation tooling used by the actor is not described in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Confluence CVE-2023-22515 zero-day exploitation begins
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says Storm-0062 exploitation of CVE-2023-22515 dates to 14 September 2023, about three weeks before disclosure [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Atlassian discloses CVE-2023-22515
campaigns.summary: Atlassian disclosed the flaw and released fixes in 8.3.3, 8.4.3 and 8.5.2; on 5 October it said customers reported attacks creating rogue administrator accounts, and the next day said it had evidence a known nation-state actor was exploiting it [S2]. CISA added the CVE to the KEV catalog on 2023-10-05 [S5].

campaigns.name: Microsoft attributes exploitation to Storm-0062
campaigns.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence named Storm-0062 (also DarkShadow, Oro0lxy) as a nation-state actor exploiting the flaw and shared four IP addresses [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: CISA/FBI/MS-ISAC advisory AA23-289A
campaigns.summary: CISA/FBI/MS-ISAC joint advisory warned of use of the flaw for initial access and advised upgrading or taking servers offline; patching does not remove an existing intruder [S5].

diamond.adversary: Microsoft-tracked nation-state cluster Storm-0062, reported by press as China-sponsored and possibly MSS-linked [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: Unauthenticated zero-day exploitation of Confluence CVE-2023-22515 to create administrator accounts [S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Four IP addresses sending exploit traffic published by Microsoft [S3]. Further infrastructure not public in gathered sources.
diamond.victim: Internet-exposed on-premises Confluence Data Center and Server 8.0.0 to 8.5.1 instances; specific victims unnamed [S2][S5].

gaps: The name 'Shadow Typhoon' could not be verified: the Microsoft naming mapping (former S1) was not seen in search results and was removed; a search found no source naming Shadow Typhoon. The title/ID name is unconfirmed.
Microsoft's original 2023-10-10 posts were not retrieved; details come from press coverage [S2][S3]. Microsoft did not state China in the notice per SecurityWeek and The Record [S2][S4].

MSS attribution rests on unnamed sources [S2]. A search summary connected Oro0lxy to Li Xiaoyu of the 2020 DOJ indictment, but this was not verified; the DOJ document was not opened and should not be relied on.
Victims, sectors, geography, objectives and post-exploitation tooling are not described in gathered sources.
No activity beyond the Sept-Oct 2023 Confluence campaign was found under Storm-0062 or Shadow Typhoon.
Overlap with other vendor clusters tracking Oro0lxy/DarkShadow was not assessed.

SecurityWeek, The Record and Dark Reading pages were seen in search results but not fetched; The Register URL was not seen in results and was removed; CISA AA23-289A is cited from the search result only.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-exposed on-premises Confluence servers are key terrain because an unauthenticated flaw let attackers create administrators [S5]. STEP 2: The actor held a roughly three-week zero-day window before disclosure, and public PoCs followed [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Template is unauthenticated exploitation leading to administrator account creation [S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is further quiet zero-day or n-day use against collaboration servers. MDCOA is mass exploitation after PoC release against unpatched DoD-adjacent contractors. Candidate indicators: unexpected administrator accounts, and traffic from the four Microsoft-listed IPs [S3][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Track patch status and exposure of on-premises Confluence for situational awareness; CVE is on the KEV catalog [S5]. (2) Patching does not remove an existing intruder, so tasking should include hunting [S5]. (3) Attribution is vendor-level only and state agency is unconfirmed, so avoid government-attribution language [S2]. (4) Coordinate exposure checks with DIB contractors and share Microsoft-listed IPs through established channels [S3].

provenance.importedSummary: The cyberattack campaign that Microsoft uncovered was launched by a China-linked hacking group called Storm-0062. According to the company, the group is launching cyberattacks by exploiting a vulnerability in the Data Center and Server editions of Confluence. Those are versions of the application that companies run on-premises.
